newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says a weaker crown could hit inflation.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says a weaker crown could hit inflation.

text.p: The deputy governor of Sweden's central bank, Lars Heikensten, said on Wednesday that a weaker crown than earlier forecast could negatively affect the inflation outlook.
However he said the Riksbank saw no reason to change its outlook for inflation in 1997.

"The new information about economic activity and price movements points to a picture of inflation in 1997 that is marginally more positive," Heikensten said in a speech to Stockholm Chamber of Commerce.
But he said in the opposite direction, the exchange rate has been somewhat weaker than expected.

"While this does not stem from what are commonly referred to as economic fundamentals, the fact remains that a weaker exchange rate -- which Sweden has now had for a quarter or so -- has effects on the picture of demand and inflation," Heikensten said.
He said the Riksbank would continue to evaluate the effects of the interest rate cuts implemented during 1996 when the bank's key rate, the repo, was cut to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent.
"The ongoing construction of monetary policy will depend on our assessment of inflation's future course, for instance in the light of incoming information," he said.
